Machina builds and operates intelligent, software-defined factories that turn design intent into complex metal structures. Our factories use AI-guided robotics to execute the full manufacturing process.
The result is production-grade metal structures delivered at the speed programs demand – from development through full-rate production, in one Machina factory.

Machina brings speed, flexibility, and design freedom to automotive manufacturing. OEMs and custom builders can customize production-grade body panels without tooling and in a fraction of the time to unlock mass customization at scale.

Machina forms and assembles thin-walled, high-temperature alloys for advanced aerospace and defense systems. We enable rapid iteration, qualification, and production of hypersonic structures, missile bodies, and restricted programs. No tooling. No delays.

Machina unlocks manufacturing for industries where metal is hard to make. From naval structures and energy systems to immersive design projects, our RoboCraftsman platform enables the rapid fabrication of precise metal structures without tooling delays or minimum volume requirements.

Machina Labs enables rapid design iteration and mass customization for the automotive industry. OEMs and custom builders can bypass tooling constraints to form production-grade metal body panels in days, not months.

Machina Labs delivers Airframe-as-a-Service through portable, Machina-operated elastic factories. We form and restore critical aircraft structures with speed and precision, supporting readiness wherever it’s needed, from program offices to forward-operating units.

Built for extreme performance, our RoboCraftsman™ platform forms thin-walled, high-temperature alloys. We support rapid iteration and qualification for hypersonics, missile bodies, and classified programs – no dedicated tooling, no delays.

Machina Labs tackles unique manufacturing challenges across industries—naval structures, energy systems, and immersive design projects. Our flexible platform forms complex metal parts fast, enabling custom fabrication without tooling delays or volume requirements

Disparate systems compromise data access, workflows and margins
As Machina Labs scaled operations to meet growing demand, they faced mounting challenges in procurement that threatened timelines, margins, and compliance.

To address these risks, Machina’s head of procurement, Robert Reeser, got in touch with Silkline. After seeing Silkline’s capabilities and intuitive UX, Robert and two of his colleagues decided to pilot the software to mitigate risk and create substantial upside.

Silkline now centralizes Machina’s purchasing data, integrating with their internal systems to ensure real-time visibility of order status from request to receipt. This allows Machina’s purchasing team to prevent delays, track orders, and make fast, informed decisions.
“Silkline makes it so easy for us to come in every day and see what's late. Being able to protect ourselves from a potential loss of $50,000 per day is transformational."
- Robert Reeser, Machina Labs' Head of Procurement
Machina’s procurement process relied on numerous manual steps, which hampered teams with administrative overhead and slowed progress on high-impact engineering and operational priorities.
“We’ve estimated that Silkline saves us 31 hours per week across engineering workflows. This adds up to more than $80,000 in cost savings per year, just looking at workflow improvements.

Silkline enables Machina to easily send RFQs to multiple suppliers, resulting in more optimal pricing and cost savings. These savings are automatically documented in their quote selection, so Machina can measure the impact of opting for specific suppliers and quotes.

As Machina Labs scaled operations to support defense and aerospace customers, maintaining rigorous supply chain accountability and cybersecurity compliance became increasingly important. Existing processes for tracking documentation made it difficult to ensure seamless alignment with the Department of Defense Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) requirements.

Silkline enhances Machina’s compliance posture by providing full traceability of orders and supplier communications, along with automated documentation to support audit readiness. With built-in SOC 2 compliance and secure US Gov Cloud data storage, Silkline ensures Machina can meet regulatory expectations without adding administrative burden.
Unified Procurement Delivers Measurable Outcomes

Machina Labs’ use of Silkline goes beyond operational gains. The unified procurement platform accelerates production momentum, reduces compliance risks, and generates significant cost savings for the company.

“Silkline has become a core part of Machina’s operations, underpinning our promise to make manufacturing parts as easy as a click of a button from anywhere in the world and for any volume,” said Reeser.

Machina Labs (hereinafter referred to as Machina) is a manufacturing platform that uses robots to form metal sheets without the use of molds, primarily developed for the U.S. Department of Defense and aerospace OEMs (manufacturers that design and produce finished aircraft).

Machina initially started as a single production unit called "RoboCraftsman," but it has now expanded its functionality into a multi-processing unit that integrates shape correction via laser scanning, trimming, drilling, welding, and heat treatment. Furthermore, it is expanding its business domain into a large-scale "Elastic Factory" concept that bundles multiple production units together.

The greatest value of this manufacturing platform lies in its strategic evolution from the stage of individually producing physical production equipment known as molds, to accumulating robot motion path data and inspection data as digital assets, thereby supporting the entire defense and aerospace production infrastructure.

In the aerospace and defense sectors, the procurement of replacement parts for aging aircraft and production lines that cannot keep up with design changes are serious issues. Machina's core value proposition against these structural constraints is to make the manufacturing process itself as rewritable as software.
